### CANDIDATE DETAIL
#### 1. Myhre syndrome  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.473)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-201451, Reactome:R-HSA-8941326)

**Proposed mechanism:** SMAD6 (HGNC:10697) —DISRUPTS→ TGF-beta signaling pathway (REACT:R-HSA-8817102); SMAD4 (HGNC:9874) —DISRUPTS→ TGF-beta signaling pathway (REACT:R-HSA-8817102); TGF-beta signaling pathway (REACT:R-HSA-8817102) —LEADS_TO→ Abnormality of the cardiovascular system (HP:0001627); TGF-beta signaling pathway (REACT:R-HSA-8817102) —LEADS_TO→ Intellectual disability (HP:0001249); TGF-beta signaling pathway (REACT:R-HSA-8817102) —LEADS_TO→ Short stature (HP:0004325); TGF-beta signaling pathway (REACT:R-HSA-8817102) —LEADS_TO→ Scoliosis (HP:0002650). Loss-of-function mutations in SMAD6 (causative for MONDO:0013902) and SMAD4 (causative for Myhre syndrome) both converge on disrupting the TGF-beta signaling pathway. Dysregulation of this pathway leads to shared phenotypic features such as cardiovascular abnormalities, intellectual disability, short stature, and scoliosis.

**How to falsify it:** Demonstration that SMAD6 and SMAD4 mutations in MONDO:0013902 and Myhre syndrome, respectively, do not converge on a shared downstream pathway or that the observed phenotypes arise from entirely distinct molecular mechanisms independent of TGF-beta signaling.

**Why it matters:** Targeting the TGF-beta signaling pathway could offer a therapeutic strategy for both MONDO:0013902 and Myhre syndrome, potentially addressing multiple shared clinical manifestations.

**Why it matters:** Targeting the TGF-beta signaling pathway or downstream effectors could offer therapeutic strategies for both juvenile polyposis and hereditary hemorrhagic telangiectasia syndrome, potentially addressing shared pathomechanisms.

Dysregulation of this pathway consequently leads to a shared set of skeletal anomalies, facial dysmorphism, short stature, and cardiac anomalies.

**How to falsify it:** If pathogenic loss-of-function variants in SMAD6 are identified in patients with MONDO:0100297, or pathogenic loss-of-function variants in BMP2 are identified in patients with MONDO:0013902, then the proposed distinct causal origins would be falsified, strengthening the hypothesis of shared downstream pathway dysregulation. _(variant: rs117171584 (SMAD6) or rs117171584 (BMP2))_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared role of BMP signaling in these two rare diseases could lead to the development of therapeutic strategies targeting this pathway for both conditions, potentially improving treatment outcomes for patients with overlapping phenotypes.

#### 5. Shprintzen-Goldberg syndrome  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.434)

**Proposed mechanism:** SMAD6 (HGNC:10750) —DISRUPTS→ TGF-beta signaling pathway (REACT:R-HSA-8963684); SKI (HGNC:10767) —DISRUPTS→ TGF-beta signaling pathway (REACT:R-HSA-8963684); TGF-beta signaling pathway (REACT:R-HSA-8963684) —LEADS_TO→ Scoliosis (HP:0002650); TGF-beta signaling pathway (REACT:R-HSA-8963684) —LEADS_TO→ Pectus excavatum (HP:0000767); TGF-beta signaling pathway (REACT:R-HSA-8963684) —LEADS_TO→ Cutis laxa (HP:0000972); TGF-beta signaling pathway (REACT:R-HSA-8963684) —LEADS_TO→ Joint hypermobility (HP:0001382). **Why it matters:** Understanding the shared mechanism involving the TGF-beta signaling pathway offers potential therapeutic targets for both MONDO:0013902 and Shprintzen-Goldberg syndrome.
